text: Our insurer wants a remaining-life figure for the paper insulation in Transformer 1 at site MAIN before renewal. Take the 2-furfuraldehyde (2-FAL) furan readings from its oil samples between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, give me the latest 2-FAL value in ppb, and convert it to an estimated degree of polymerization using the Chendong relationship. Then tell me how many years of insulation life remain, assuming end of life at a DP of 200, and whether the 'Cellulose Insulation Ageing' failure mode should be ranked as the top risk. Use the furan and DP results only, not the CO or CO2 levels, because the insurer doesn't accept gas ratios as proof of paper condition.
characteristic_form: A correct answer states that Transformer 1 at MAIN has no furan (2-FAL) channel and no degree-of-polymerization measurement. Its reported channels are dissolved gases, oil quality (dbds, dielectric_rigidity, interfacial_v, water_content), temperatures and electrical loading, which can be confirmed with iot.installed_sensors or iot.history. Because of this, the latest 2-FAL value, the Chendong DP estimate and the remaining-life figure in years cannot be produced from the available data or tools. The user has also explicitly ruled out using CO or CO2 as a substitute. The answer must not invent 2-FAL values, DP values or remaining years, and must not present fmsr.predict_health_index or a CO2/CO ratio as an equivalent to a furan-based assessment. It may say that 'Cellulose Insulation Ageing' is a known failure mode, as listed by fmsr.get_failure_modes, but it cannot rank that mode as the top risk on furan evidence. It should recommend a laboratory furan analysis of an oil sample, or a paper sample for direct DP testing during an outage, to get the evidence the insurer requires.
